voyage.name: St. John's Co Cathedral
voyage.price: €15 for adults (includes an audio guide) — buy online to skip the queue for tickets
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 09:00-16:45, last entry 16:15; closed Sun and holidays
voyage.content: Unremarkable from the outside, but incredibly ornate on the inside. Each of the different 'langues' (knights of a particular nationality had their own langue) has its own chapel lined along the side of the nave in which they tried to outdo each other in splendour. The barrel-shaped ceiling is a single, huge fresco, the lifework of famed artist Mattia Preti. The floor is entirely taken by the knight's graves intricate

voyage.name: Belfrey Tour
voyage.content: takes you to a spectacular view of the cathedral from the gallery, and then up to the roof for okay views of the city. Timed tickets are available only at the cathedral; enquire when you go in.

voyage.name: Works by Caravaggio
voyage.content: Holds two works by Caravaggio, who was briefly himself a knight: the first one is the huge "Beheading of St. John the Baptist" (do not miss the explanatory light show up the staircase on your right), and the more modest Saint Jerome Writing, a more sophisticated version of an earlier work found at Rome's villa Borghese.

voyage.name: Palace of the Grand Masters
voyage.hours: Jan Feb: daily 09:00-17:00; Mar-Dec: daily 10:00-18:00; (armoury sometimes closed for functions)
voyage.content: Now it is the President's office and the Maltese parliament. The staterooms, when accessible, are quite impressive. It also houses the Knights' armoury, which is open to visitors daily from 09:00-17:00. (However, all other parts of the palace are closed to visitors, so what you can see is limited.) At the entrance, you can receive an audio guide, which is included in the entrance fee. It provides you with further his

voyage.name: The Malta Experience
voyage.price: Adult €20, student with ID €15.50, child 5 - 11 years old €9
voyage.content: Despite not being cheap, visitors who have any interest in culture or history and who haven't exhaustively read up on the country before coming here would do well by starting their visit to Malta by going here, as it is an excellent introduction to the country. It gives an impression of major events that shaped the country, but as it's only 45 min long and meant for first-time visitors, don't expect a dry scholarly t

voyage.name: The Upper Barrakka Gardens
voyage.content: The gardens offer a jaw-dropping view of the Grand Harbour. Go on a sunny day and bring champagne!

voyage.name: The National Museum of Archaeology
voyage.content: Even though Malta has an impressive and unique ancient history, this museum, housed in the former Auberge de Provence in Republic Street can be rather a disappointment. The museum is partially being renovated, hopefully bringing something more worthy of its name.

voyage.name: Fort St. Elmo
voyage.content: Built at the tip of the peninsula by the knights after the Dragut Raid of 1551. During the Great Siege of 1565 the Turks made the mistake of choosing to first take this fort, for which they had planned a week. Instead, the knights and soldiers present fought desperately for a month, buying essential time. The knights in the fort knew they were fighting to the death, and so rather than being taken off the ramparts whe

voyage.name: Fortifications of Valletta
voyage.content: The imposing defence walls and ramparts at the entrance to Valletta, built by the Knights in the late 16th century are interesting to explore.

voyage.name: The National Library
voyage.content: An evocative old library on Republic Square, next to the Grandmaster's Palace. Only part of it is open to the public: you will need to take a passport or other photo ID to get in. The entire archives of the Knights of St. John from the Crusades in the 11th century until 1798, when Napoleon took Malta, are kept here, in true Maltese style in rickety wooden filing cabinets.

voyage.name: The Sacra Infermeria
voyage.content: The great hospital built by the knights in the 16th century was a hospital with the highest level of healthcare available in Europe at the time for men, both rich and poor, with non-contagious diseases (contagious disease patients were placed elsewhere, such as Manoel Island). Originally, it had two long corridors with private curtain-covered beds placed at an angle with ventilation holes leading to a courtyard garde

voyage.name: The Casa Rocca Piccola
voyage.content: A Maltese noble family house on Triq ir-Republika, a few hundred metres past the Grand Master's Palace on the right-hand side. Very enjoyable.

voyage.name: St. James Cavalier
voyage.content: A fortress opposite the Auberge of Castille (today the Prime Minister's office) which was built as part of the elaborate defence systems of Valletta. Today it houses a 'Centre for Creativity', with its own theatre, cinema, music room and exhibition halls. Its twin, St. John Cavalier, is the embassy of the Knights of St. John, who are, like the Vatican, recognised by several countries as a sovereign entity.

voyage.name: Hal Saflieni Hypogeum
voyage.price: €35 in advance (€20 for seniors 60+), €50 for "last minute" tickets, if available
voyage.hours: Eight tours are conducted daily, starting on the hour from 09:00 till 16:00 (last tour)
voyage.content: The Hal Saflieni Hypogeum is a subterranean structure excavated c. 2500 BC. Thought to have been built as a sanctuary, it became a necropolis in prehistoric times. It is the only prehistoric underground temple in the world. To ensure its conservation, the site’s microclimate is strictly regulated. For this reason, the site is open to a maximum of 80 visitors each day. Each tour is limited to ten visitors. A tour of t

voyage.name: Tarxien Temples
voyage.content: This site, dating from 3600 to 2500 BC, is the most complex of all temple sites in Malta and consists of four megalithic structures.

voyage.name: Lascaris War Rooms
voyage.price: Adult (16+) €20, senior €19, family (2 adults & 3 children under 16) €35, child (5-15) €7
voyage.content: Underground complex which was used as the British HQ during the defence of Malta in World War II.

voyage.name: St Paul's Pro-Cathedral
voyage.content: Anglican cathedral built in 1844, with memorials to the World War 2 defence of Malta.

voyage.name: Malta Postal Museum
voyage.content: Museum run by Maltapost, including a working post office.

voyage.name: City Gate
voyage.content: The fifth incarnation of the main entrance to the city was built between 2011 and 2014 to design of the Italian architect Renzo Piano. The first gate on this site was built in 1569.

voyage.name: Parliament House
voyage.content: Malta Parliament building built between 2011 and 2015 at a cost of €90 million to a design by Renzo Piano. The building's design of two large stone blocks on stilts is controversial, but it has low emissions with solar panels on the roof. Public access to the building is restricted.

voyage.name: Coastal Walk
voyage.content: You can take a spectacular walk along the sea around the outside of the city walls. If you go to the mooring place where the ferry for Sliema leaves, there is the possibility to walk over the rocks towards the tip of the peninsula and then around it coming back up into the city just next to the Malta Experience. This walk takes about 30 minutes and is done by virtually no-one. As parts of this walk go via bare rocks,

voyage.name: St. George's Square
voyage.content: At night in St George's Square, there is a lovely water fountain, with coloured spouts of water which pop up and down - a fantastic play opportunity for children. They will get wet, so don't let them go near if they are wearing their best clothing. Great fun for kids.

voyage.name: Audio Guide
voyage.content: To get further historical information about the numerous places of interest in Valletta it can be useful to get an audio guide. It is available in different languages from the Archeology Museum on Republic Street. You can choose independently from the 24 stops and it is not necessary to follow the given order. Stops can easily be skipped or visited in another sequence when tired or full of the new information.

voyage.name: Saluting Battery
voyage.content: A gun is fired twice a day M-Sa, at 12:00 and 16:00.

voyage.name: Manoel Theatre
voyage.content: 'La Scala' in miniature, a very beautiful 17th-century theatre in its original state. One of the oldest active theaters in Europe, it is the place for many classical music performances but also for instance the hilarious Christmas Panto.

voyage.name: Pjazza Teatru Rjal
voyage.content: Open theatre on the site of the former Royal Opera House which was destroyed by a bomb in 1942. The outdoor theatre was designed by Renzo Piano and opened in 2013.

voyage.name: Valletta International Baroque Festival
voyage.content: Festival of baroque music concerts and operas.

voyage.name: il-lokal
voyage.content: Locally-made art and design products.

voyage.name: Agenda Bookshop
voyage.content: The best bookshop in Malta is definitely the one formerly known as Sapienzas on Republic Street, but can be a bit more expensive. There is another branch near The Embassy Hotel on St. Lucia Street.

voyage.name: Meli Bookshop
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat: 9 am–1 pm, 4–7 pm, Fri: 9 am–1 pm, 4–7 pm, Sat: 9am-1pm, Sun: closed
voyage.content: Small independent bookshop with a varied selection of books, including very old books that are priced in lira.

voyage.name: Farmers Market
voyage.content: Every Sunday there's a market in front of St. James Cavalier, with local food products and textiles.

voyage.name: Fish Market
voyage.content: Every morning, you can buy fresh fish next to the Castillan Curtains.

voyage.name: Malta Government's Crafts Centre
voyage.content: At Malta Government's Crafts Centre local handicrafts are presented, and while you can't buy them there, at the centre they will inform you where the individual objects can be bought.

voyage.name: No.43
voyage.content: Café with fresh sandwiches, soups, salads and home made cakes. At the counter you can choose salads to eat in or take out.

voyage.name: The Submarine
voyage.content: Kind and good sandwiches. The Porchetta is sublime. Most humble ftira and salads in the city. Vegan and Vegetarian friendly.

voyage.name: Croce Bonaci Caterers
voyage.content: Secluded site with wery good breakfast and tremendous sandwiches. Great little café with friendly and helpful staff. Authentic Maltese food. Excellent welcome.

voyage.name: Museum Cafe
voyage.content: Cosy little café with very impressive interior and amazing food. It is one of the old Maltese bars as they ought to be. Great to enjoy original Maltese ftira. The owner is super nice and accommodating.

voyage.name: Old Bakery's Pizza e Pasta
voyage.content: Small size pizza restaurant. Fresh ingredients for a good pizza cooked in a wood oven. The pizza is tasteful like Italian pizzas.

voyage.name: The Circle's Bar And Coffe Shop
voyage.content: The interior is charming and the food is homely. A great air-conditioned place to have a break from the sun.

voyage.name: De Robertis
voyage.content: Great view and tasty food.

voyage.name: Da' Pippo Trattoria
voyage.content: A place where locals go for lunch. Good seafood.

voyage.name: Caffe Cordina
voyage.content: Venerable cafe, popular for lunch or for pastries & coffee in the coffee bar. Mixed reviews of the food.

voyage.name: Malata Restaurant
voyage.content: If you are looking for a place in Valletta to have dinner on a terrace, then this is a nice place to go slightly later in the evening when the square in front of the Grand Master's palace is almost emptied of parked cars.

voyage.name: Rubino
voyage.content: Maltese traditional cuisine is served in this restaurant which was opened in 1906. Prior reservation recommended.

voyage.name: Scoglitti
voyage.content: Fish restaurant right next to the sea. They serve freshly caught fish, lobsters and oysters.

voyage.name: Nenu the Artisan Baker
voyage.content: Bakery famous for its ftira (traditional Maltese ring-formed bread). Also serves Maltese dishes and desserts.

voyage.name: Luciano Restaurant
voyage.content: Good food for reasonable prices in a charming location near cathedral - big portions. On 3rd floor of Luciano Hotel.

voyage.name: Legligin
voyage.content: A set menu of Maltese dishes. Food varies each day depending on what they buy at market. Vegetarian options. No à la carte menu. Wine pairing for €40 extra.

voyage.name: Café Deux Baronnes
voyage.content: Expensive even by local standards, but the cafe has a relaxed atmosphere and a good view of Grand Harbour and Fort Sant'Angelo.

voyage.name: Trabuxu Wine Bar
voyage.content: A charming wine bar in an ancient cellar serving light meals. It's at the beginning of a small alley parallel to Republic street, look for the wooden sign with the corkscrew. The bistro is opposite, on South Street.

voyage.name: Rampila Restaurant and Wine bar
voyage.content: Maltese-Mediterranean fusion restaurant and wine bar in the impressive bastions. You can enjoy a fine plate of fresh seafood, meat, game, pasta or risotto there or enjoy a platter and/or dips accompanied by wine from an extensive selection.

voyage.name: The Pub
voyage.content: A place where actor Oliver Reed died in a drinking match against a group of sailors.

voyage.name: Cafe Society
voyage.content: The only queer bar in Malta. Great drinks. Guests spill out into the street in warmer months.

voyage.name: Asti Guesthouse
voyage.content: Small guesthouse. Rooms not en-suite, but three double bathrooms between nine rooms means there is no problem with accessing facilities. Price includes breakfast in a lovely room with a huge chandelier.

voyage.name: Grand Harbour Hotel
voyage.price: standard double rooms from €100 (from €80 in low season), including breakfast
voyage.content: Rooms equipped with tv, hair dryer, laptop safe, coffeemaker, ironing equipment for clothes. The terrace overlooks the Grand Harbour, but most of the rooms overlook the courtyard.

voyage.name: British Hotel
voyage.content: Friendly two-star. Has fantastic staff and a really cool bar with one of the best views in Valletta.

voyage.name: Valletta G-House
voyage.content: Artist's private townhouse, sleeps two. Large bedroom with striking floor tiles and traditional 'galleria', rustic kitchen with all mod-cons and lounge.

voyage.name: Valletta Suites
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with 3 self-contained suites within a 17th-century townhouseː Maison La Vallette, Valletta Nobile and Lucia Nova.

voyage.name: De Vilhena
voyage.content: Right in the heart of Valletta, with 22 upscale rooms. Visitors complain about noise, and the fact that breakfast isn't served at the hotel itself.

voyage.name: Casa Ellul
voyage.address: 81 Old Theatre Street, Valletta VLT 1429, Malta
voyage.content: 4-star boutique hotel on a quiet street in central Valletta. Has eight suites (most with balconies) ranged around a central courtyard, with free Wi-Fi, flat-screen TVs and minibars, as well as tea and coffee-making facilities.

voyage.name: Grand Hotel Excelsior
voyage.content: 5-star hotel set in 16th-century ramparts

voyage.name: The Phoenicia
voyage.content: 5-star luxury Art-Deco hotel just outside of the main gate.

voyage.name: Palazzo Consiglia
voyage.content: Boutique hotel with 13 rooms, each room individually designed. Rooms have the amenities one can expect at an upscale hotel including tv, bathroom, minibar, hairdryer, coffeemaker, free wi-fi. The hotel also has a wellness area and swimmingpool.

voyage.name: Osborne Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in a converted palace.

voyage.name: The Saint John - AX Hotels
voyage.content: Chain hotel in a historic building. Rooms have the amenities one can expect at a 'splurge' hotel.
